editorial.headline: Democrats favored for the House; Senate control remains close
editorial.summary: Two weeks before Election Day, published forecasts favor a Democratic House majority and give Democrats a narrow Senate edge. A working central scenario is 235 Democratic and 200 Republican House seats, and a 51–49 Democratic Senate caucus advantage. These are DDHQ’s projected seat centers adopted as an editorial baseline, not promised results or a new Midterm Watch probability model.
editorial.senate_call: Very close, with a slight Democratic edge
editorial.probability_policy: Display publisher probabilities separately with publisher, timestamp and methodology. Do not average the models or call the difference between their point forecasts a confidence interval.
editorial.rating_policy: House: compare DDHQ October 20 with original Cook October 16. Senate/governors: compare DDHQ with the dated UVA source. Same favored party: use the less confident label; any toss-up or opposite favored parties: Toss-up. Executive offices compare the dated Jacobson assessment with the October 20 Horizon category; no publisher numerical probability is adopted. Legislative assessments remain attributed to Jacobson. No numerical odds are fabricated for unpolled courts or propositions.
forecast_limitations: Models share some polls; agreement is not independent statistical confirmation.
DDHQ race pages describe a blend of 30% fundamentals, 45% polls and 25% markets. Its forecasts are not polling-only estimates.
Poliwave says its correlated model has not been historically calibrated and uses simplified ranked-choice/runoff treatment.
Statewide and national polling errors can move together.
The 51–49 Senate scenario refers to caucus alignment; newly elected independents may affect control.

site_findings.title: Registration map uses a generic late-registration message
site_findings.evidence: Homepage titles for states including PA, TX and SD say same-day rules may still apply even though the site dataset marks late_registration=none.
site_findings.recommendation: Render state-specific action text using method and exception fields; suppress the generic caveat where ordinary same-day registration is unavailable.
site_findings.verification: Check PA/TX/SD against CA/NC/NE at the same date.

site_findings.title: One registration date hides later routes
site_findings.evidence: The scalar date loses Illinois online October 18, Nebraska in-person October 23, Louisiana online October 13 and Hawaii online Election Day.
site_findings.recommendation: Use separate online, mail and in-person fields, with receipt/postmark type and proof/location notes.
site_findings.verification: A passed mail deadline must not disable a later valid method.

site_findings.title: Freshness badges must distinguish checks from data vintage
site_findings.evidence: Homepage/data page say generated October 10; current capture is October 20.
site_findings.recommendation: Store source publication, poll fieldwork, actual source check, dataset build and browser render times separately.
site_findings.verification: Never update source_retrieved_at merely because a page rebuilds.

site_findings.title: Calendar coverage chart is incomplete by design
site_findings.evidence: Home chart explicitly counts only 18 reviewed jurisdiction primary records and shows zeros for earlier months.
site_findings.recommendation: Move it to a labeled archive section or replace it with a general-election deadline timeline.
site_findings.verification: Avoid presenting missing primary coverage as zero elections.

site_findings.title: Canonical and structured-data opportunity
site_findings.evidence: Full HTML sample: homepage, PA/NC/WI state desks and About contained no canonical link or JSON-LD. Robots and sitemap were reachable.
site_findings.recommendation: Add self-referencing canonicals and truthful WebSite/Organization, BreadcrumbList and Dataset metadata. Add dateModified only for actual changes.
site_findings.verification: Inspect served head and validate JSON-LD after deployment; search-engine selected canonicals were not measured.

site_findings.title: A forecast section needs its own editorial standard
site_findings.evidence: The current methodology covers official dates and human review; no forecasting method is stated.
site_findings.recommendation: Keep official voting facts separate from polling, editorial ratings and attributed model outputs. Publish the comparison rule and a correction log.
site_findings.verification: Every forecast card identifies producer, data time and uncertainty.

site_findings.title: Election-night states need explicit status
site_findings.evidence: Current site is a calendar, with no inspected live results feed.
site_findings.recommendation: Prepare awaiting polls / counting / projected / certified states; attach a named call provider and official certification source.
site_findings.verification: A forecast must never automatically become a race call.

site_findings.title: Accessibility and mobile improvements
site_findings.evidence: Maps and tiles are the principal navigation in the inspected content; visual interaction was not functionally tested.
site_findings.recommendation: Offer searchable text tables, keyboard-accessible state controls, explicit date labels and non-color status cues; test contrast and touch targets.
site_findings.verification: Check keyboard, screen reader and a 390px viewport before release.

site_findings.title: Organic-search expansion
site_findings.evidence: Current titles and descriptions already identify 2026 and November 3. No rank, traffic or speed measurements were collected.
site_findings.recommendation: Add distinct Senate, House, governors, polling and how-to-vote routes; keep useful state pages canonical and link them to related races.
site_findings.verification: Check unique titles, internal links and indexability; measure performance separately.
